processing_steps.method: high-frequency vacuum induction melting and casting into ingot
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Melted in a high-frequency vacuum induction furnace with a 50 kg capacity and cast into an ingot with a diameter of 150 mm.
Ingots homogenized at 1200 °C for 5 h before hot rolling.
Hot rolled into rods with a diameter of 16 mm, then air-cooled to room temperature.
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: ingot Ø150 mm hot rolled into rods of Ø16 mm

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot-rolled rods solution-treated at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching; this is the final state used for tensile tests, Charpy impact toughness and EBSD/TEM characterization.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD system attached to a FEI Quanta 650 field emission gun SEM; operating voltage 20 kV, step size 0.5 μm; specimens mechanically ground and electro-polished in 7% Nital at room temperature; grain size by linear intercept with 15° misorientation criterion using Channel 5 software
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the Mn-25 steel: austenite grain size 18.8 ± 1.3 μm, ferrite volume fraction 0.65% with ferrite grain size 4.5 ± 0.7 μm, twin boundary fraction 52.6%; grains coarsen with increasing Mn content and ferrite is nearly absent.
characterization_methods.purpose: determine phase distribution, grain size and twin boundary fraction of the solution-treated steels

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Tecnai G2 F20 S-TWIN TEM operated at 200 kV; thin foils prepared by twin-jet electro-polishing in a mixture of 10% perchloric acid and 90% ethanol at 20 V and −20 °C
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the Mn-25 steel the average κ-carbide size is about 5 nm (5.0 ± 2.1 nm), uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix; the κ/austenite orientation relationship is (001)κ || (001)γ and the interface is coherent.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: dark-field images taken along [001]γ zone axis using a κ-carbide diffraction spot
characterization_methods.purpose: characterize the size, distribution and crystallography of κ-carbides
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) dark-field imaging with SAED

analytical_models.equation_role: σTS = σUTS(1 + UE); maximum true stress just before necking (point of crack nucleation)
σFS = σEF/(1 − A); engineering fracture stress divided by (1 − area reduction)
σ_shear = α f^(1/2) d_Car^(1/2); strengthening contribution of κ-carbides to the austenite phase via particle shearing (rather than Orowan bypass)
analytical_models.model_note: A constant slope of 97.1 MPa/nm^1/2 was obtained from the linear fit of yield strength vs d_Car^0.5 for all compositions; particle shear strengthening remains active up to κ-carbide sizes of 50 nm.

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: σTS ≈ 1350 MPa and σFS ≈ 2150 MPa, evaluated from Eqns. (1) and (2), were found to be nearly constant for all investigated compositions and did not vary significantly with alloying content.

interfaces.interface_notes: Orientation relationship between κ-carbides and austenite (γ): (001)κ || (001)γ.
interfaces.slip_behavior: κ-carbides are sheared by dislocations (particle shear strengthening) rather than bypassed by an Orowan mechanism; shear deformation facilitates glide of dislocations across κ-carbide shear planes and lowers the work hardening rate.

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed grains with abundant Σ3 twin boundaries (twin boundary fraction 52.6%)

precipitates.distribution: uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix

structures.overall_structure: After solution treatment at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching, the Mn-25 (Fe25Mn11Al1C) steel is nearly single-phase FCC austenite with a small fraction of BCC ferrite (f_Bcc = 0.65%) and uniformly distributed κ-carbides; the austenite grains have coarsened to about 18.8 μm and twin boundaries are abundant.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: MTS tensile machine; two solution-treated specimens tested and the reported data is the average value of two specimens
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: round tensile specimen, gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm, tensile axis parallel to the rod axis

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain behaviour of the Fe(x)Mn11Al1C steels after 1050 °C/2 h solution treatment is shown in Fig. 2(b); corresponding true stress-strain and work-hardening-rate curves in Fig. 8(b).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: MTS impact tester (500 J capacity); two solution-treated specimens tested and the reported data is the average value of two specimens
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Charpy impact specimen 55 mm long, 10 × 10 mm cross-section, V-notch 2 mm deep; V-notch perpendicular to the rod axis

fracture_toughness.note: Charpy V-notch impact energy (Akv-40) measured at −40 °C

unmapped_findings: Twin boundary fraction f_Tw of the Mn-25 (Fe25Mn11Al1C) steel after 1050 °C/2 h solution treatment is 52.6% (Table 3).
For the Fe(x)Mn11Al1C series the yield strength decreased from 896 MPa (Mn-20) to 401 MPa (Mn-35) and total elongation increased from 28.5% to 60% as Mn increased from 20% to 35% (Fig. 2b).
κ-carbide size in the Fe(x)Mn11Al1C series decreased from about 18 nm (20%Mn) to 5 nm (25%Mn), 3 nm (30%Mn) and 2 nm (35%Mn) (Fig. 4(e–h)).
The work hardening rate increases with Mn content, reaching a maximum of around 2300 MPa in the 35%Mn steel; the 25%Mn sample is intermediate between the 20%Mn and 35%Mn extremes (Fig. 8b).

Paper-wide linear fits (Fig. 7) against the square root of κ-carbide size d_Car^0.5 (d_Car in nm, stresses in MPa): R_p0.2 = 478 + 97.1 d_Car^0.5; R_m = 786 + 54.6 d_Car^0.5; A_5 = 64.5 − 6.445 d_Car^0.5; Z = 78 − 3.85 d_Car^0.5.
For all investigated low-density steel compositions σTS ≈ 1350 MPa and σFS ≈ 2150 MPa were nearly independent of alloying content and microstructure (Table 2).
The present sample (Mn-25) is one of the intermediate-Mn members of the Fe(x)Mn11Al1C series; the paper states that higher Mn content improves impact toughness while lowering yield strength.
